chapter: Carnegie Hall and the touring years
title: Atlantic hits, rock 'n' roll package shows and Bill Haley
summary: He recorded more hits, toured with Ruth Brown, and met Bill Haley, who covered 'Shake, Rattle and Roll'.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So we...we started...we started recording that. After that, we made "Corrine Corrina," "Sweet Sixteen," "Honey Hush." 'N' lemme see...so many a numbers we made. "Chained Love." We made a whole lot of numbers, so I was the hottest thing out on the block. Ruth Brown was workin' for Atlantic Recording Company. She had...she had a number out, "Mama, You Treat Your Daughter Mean." So I got acquainted with her, an' we went on rock 'n' roll shows. We'd get...fourteen or twenty acts and go down South and play rock 'n' roll shows. We played auditoriums. That's when Bill Haley picked up my number "Shake, Rattle and Roll," and he made it. That started all over again, y'know.

I never had met him, so, finally, I met him in New York City. Him and his band. So he took me out, and we had dinner, an' we had us a ball. So he said he was goin' to take me on some o' his shows wit' him. So we had LaVerne La Baker, had The Drifters, the Fives (?). We had a bunch of 'em...blues singers. So we all took off to Australia... went to Australia. I left here. We come to California, and then we left and went to Australia. So I come here to see my mother, and then I... I promised I was gonna buy her a home. She lived out at Ninety-Ninth and Central. Had an apartment upstairs over the place...had a joint called the Blue Room Chicken Shack. So I went out there and met my mother an' we had a ball. So then I started lookin' for a place for my mother.
